map_features.note: Editorial Coral Sea point offshore northern Queensland on the northward branch described in the source; naming extent around the Gulf of Papua remains unsettled.
map_features.positional_uncertainty: not quantified; no observed current core or path

map_features.note: Broad Hiri naming convention: northward Australian boundary branch from an OSW 15 S bifurcation approach, clockwise around the Gulf of Papua entrance, to an OSW eastern Louisiade approach. Excludes closed gyre return circuits, direct mid-basin Solomon inflow, EAC, downstream New Guinea currents and eddy excursions. Narrower literature uses Hiri only south of PNG and proposes Gulf of Papua Current for the connected boundary system; no alias merge or complete system extent admitted.
map_features.spatial_geometry_method: WGS84 geodesic legs densified at <=10 km as in the existing reference-route state join; planar relation to coarse masked OSW display polygons.

original_regional_context.display_aria_label: Hiri under Hughes historical southern-Papua convention: 50 km reported local e-folding scale in July 1987. Not full current width or annual range.
original_regional_context.display_caption: July 1987, TEW287 A87: approximately 50 km author-reported decay scale. A decay scale describes how rapidly the cross-section velocity decreases; it is not a full edge-to-edge width.
original_regional_context.display_method_note: Historical Hiri/Coral Sea NGCU source convention; northern modern NGCU is not assigned this value. July 1987 and July 1990 are different years and reaches, not seasonal extrema. Width depth support and paired boundaries unresolved.
original_regional_context.historical_name_scope: Hughes introduction p13 / PDF29 calls chapter 3 Hiri Current. Chapter3 uses NGCU for a broader Coral Sea circulation under presumed Vitiaz connectivity. Only this southern-Papua study reach is indexed under Hiri; no modern north-coast NGCU alias or whole-circulation equivalence admitted.
